hints: Focus on what controls SN1, the stability of the carbocation formed when the C-X bond breaks in the slow step.
Check each structure for substitution, compounds 1 and 2 both have three alkyl groups on the carbon bearing the halogen, so they are tertiary.
Compare that with compound 3 where the Br is on a $\text{CH}_2$ group, then decide which combination favours formation of a stable carbocation.
walkthrough:
**Recall SN1 versus SN2**

SN1 hydrolysis goes in two steps. The slow, rate-determining step is loss of halide to form a carbocation.

$$\text{R}_3\text{C-X} \rightarrow \text{R}_3\text{C}^+ + \text{X}^-$$
This means anything that stabilises the carbocation speeds up SN1.

**Link stability to structure**

Alkyl groups donate electron density and stabilise a positive charge. So stability follows:

$$\text{tertiary} > \text{secondary} > \text{primary}$$
Tertiary halogenoalkanes strongly favour SN1, primary halogenoalkanes strongly favour SN2.

**Classify compounds 1, 2 and 3**

Compound 1 is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CCl}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The C-Cl carbon is joined to three carbons, so tertiary.

Compound 2 is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CBr}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The C-Br carbon is also joined to three carbons, so tertiary.

Compound 3 is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$. The C-Br carbon is $\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$, joined to only one carbon, so primary.

**Make the final deduction**

Compounds 1 and 2 can form stable tertiary carbocations, so they tend to react by SN1. Compound 3 would form a very unstable primary carbocation, so it reacts by SN2 instead.

options.A: Incorrect. This suggests all three react by SN1. Compounds 1 and 2 do, but compound 3 is primary ($\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$) and cannot form a stable carbocation, so it follows SN2.
options.B: Correct. Compounds 1 and 2 are both tertiary halogenoalkanes. Loss of $\text{Cl}^-$ or $\text{Br}^-$ gives a stable tertiary carbocation, which is the hallmark of SN1 hydrolysis.
options.C: Incorrect. While compound 2 is tertiary and SN1, compound 3 is primary. Pairing a correct tertiary compound with a primary compound that prefers SN2 makes this combination wrong.
options.D: Incorrect. Compound 1 alone is incomplete. Compound 2 is also tertiary ($\text{CBr}$ with three alkyl groups) and is just as able to react by SN1, the Br being an even better leaving group than Cl.
